column2: Software Development using AI
UG

This course examines modern AI-native software development, where developers collaborate with coding agents. It covers how to define intent, provide effective context, structure development workflows, and coordinate AI tools. Students gain practical experience designing and evaluating agent-assisted software development processes. Target students build upon strong programming and software development fundamentals to engage in automated testing and agent-assisted coding workflows. Upon completing the course, students are able to operate coding agents using orchestration frameworks, implement agent skills and tool integrations via the Model Context Protocol, construct executable specifications from requirements documents, analyse iterative development loops with log evidence, and evaluate AI-native software development workflows for multi-component applications. The course is taught through lectures, tutorials, and practical laboratory sessions complemented by hands-on projects.

column2: Laboratory Exercise

Configure a local agent orchestration framework (such as LangGraph) on student development machines. Set up environment variables, configure API keys, and verify connectivity by executing a basic single-agent prompt template.

Run a pre-configured coding agent on a provided Python repository to resolve simple bugs. Students must configure static analysis tools to ensure that the agent's output produces no warnings and passes all public tests.

Implement a multi-agent system where a coder agent and a tester agent collaborate. The coder agent generates code to solve a programming task, while the tester agent executes tests and provides feedback iteratively.
Translate natural language user stories and requirements documents into Gherkin feature files for a specified use-case, ensuring complete coverage of all functional requirements.
Implement step definitions in Python for the Gherkin feature files created in Week 4. Execute the specifications to validate system behavior and verify that all tests pass.
Implement a basic server-side Model Context Protocol (MCP) connection handler. Define custom data schemas to expose local database schemas to an external agent.
Open lab session for catching up on previous labs, debugging MCP handlers, and preparing for mid-semester evaluations. No new content is introduced.
Integrate custom tools into an MCP server and implement secure execution of these tools using a Docker-based sandbox environment to prevent unauthorized system access.
Trace the execution of an iterative coding agent loop using LangSmith. Analyze execution logs to map the agent's decision steps and identify state transitions.
Analyze execution logs of 100 automated agent runs to identify, categorize, and document at least three distinct failure modes, providing supporting log evidence.
Debug a failing multi-agent workflow by modifying prompt templates and tool schemas based on failure analysis, ensuring the workflow successfully completes the task.
Deploy a multi-component AI-native application consisting of a frontend, an orchestrator, and multiple MCP tools using Docker Compose.
Conduct a structured evaluation of the deployed workflow, writing a design justification report that maps each design decision against stated system requirements.
